questions.q: Why does Priya Nair's Key Accounts role report directly to Monica Reyes instead of through Derek Oyelaran?
options: Because Salesforce role hierarchies cannot have more than two levels
Because Oyelaran has no profile that allows managing other roles
Because Nair does not use the Sales Manager profile
Because Key Accounts deals are large and sensitive, and Cascade doesn't want the New Business manager seeing them by default
questions.explain: The lesson states this placement is deliberate: Key Accounts deals are large and sensitive, so they stay out of Oyelaran's default role-hierarchy visibility by placing Nair directly under Reyes.

questions.q: What Organization-Wide Default does every object in this security model use, and why?
options: Public Read/Write, so every rep can edit any record for speed
Private, because deal values, renewal data, and unqualified Leads should start locked down before role hierarchy or sharing rules add anything back
Public Read Only, because reporting requires org-wide visibility
Controlled by Parent, because every object is a child of Account
questions.explain: The lesson sets every object -- Account/Contact, Opportunity, Lead, Installation Project, Service Contract -- to Private OWD, explicitly because this sensitive data should start locked down before anything is added back.

questions.q: What problem does the "Service & Installation team -> read access on Opportunity" sharing rule solve?
options: It lets installers edit Opportunity amounts directly
It grants installers delete access on Leads
It gives Marcus Webb's installers visibility into the won Opportunity behind an Installation Project, since they don't report into the sales role hierarchy
It hides Opportunities from the Service team entirely
questions.explain: The lesson explains installers need to see the won Opportunity behind an Installation Project they're working, but since Service doesn't report into the sales branch, role hierarchy alone doesn't grant that -- the sharing rule closes the gap.

questions.q: What is the difference between what a profile controls and what the role hierarchy controls?
options: A profile controls record visibility; the role hierarchy controls object and field access
They control the exact same thing and are redundant
A profile controls what a user is allowed to do (object/field access); the role hierarchy controls which records roll up to which managers
A profile only applies to custom objects; role hierarchy only applies to standard objects
questions.explain: The lesson frames these as two independent systems: profiles answer 'what can they do,' while role hierarchy (along with OWD and sharing rules) answers 'which records can they see.'

questions.q: Why does this lesson design the full security model before Lesson 11 implements any of it in Setup?
options: Because Setup requires a pre-approved document before profiles can be created
Because role hierarchy, profiles, and sharing rules are hard to unwind once users already rely on them, so settling the design against the finished data model avoids ad hoc decisions mid-build
Because Salesforce limits how many profiles can be created per day
Because sharing rules cannot be created after any records exist
questions.explain: The lesson states directly that these structures are hard to unwind once users are relying on them, so designing the full picture now means Lesson 11 is translation into Setup rather than ad hoc decisions discovered mid-build.
